title: Kummer charts for invertible-order torsors on a regular principal divisor complement
statement: Let $i:U\to L$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $G$ a finite group and $W\to U$ a finite etale $G$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Let $R$ be a commutative regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], $\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}R\to L$ any morphism, and $f\in R$ a nonzerodivisor with regular quotient $R/(f)$. Assume $|G|$ is invertible in $R$. Suppose an isomorphism $\beta:U\times_L\operatorname{Spec}R\simeq D(f)$ [def-pc-fibre-product] satisfies $\beta;\iota_{D(f)}=\operatorname{pr}_2$. For every $y\in\operatorname{Spec}R$ there exist a commutative ring $S$, an etale $\psi:\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $z$ with $\psi(z)=y$, $m\ge0$, $g\in S$, and positive invertible integers $e_k$ indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}m$. The rings $S$ and $S/(g)$ are regular and multiplication by $g$ is injective. Put $B=\prod_k S[T]/(T^{e_k}-g)$, $N=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $q:N\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ the structure map, and $V=D(\operatorname{algebraMap}_{S,B}(g))$. There exists $\gamma:W\times_L\operatorname{Spec}S\simeq V$ with $\gamma;\iota_V;q=\operatorname{pr}_2$, where the map $\operatorname{Spec}S\to L$ is $\psi;\varphi$ and $W\to L$ is the torsor map followed by $i$. All rings and schemes lie in one universe and $G$ in the next. Neither $L$ nor $U$ is required to be smooth or a trait family; zero factors are allowed.

proof.text: Identify U times_L Spec R with D(f) using beta, and base change the torsor to D(f). At each generic point of V(f), regularity of R and R/(f) and injectivity of multiplication by f give a DVR local ring. Connected components of the generic torsor have Galois groups equal to their stabilizers. By 09EB, ramification and residue degrees divide the stabilizer order and hence the unit order of G. Therefore their ramification is tame in codimension one.

Apply 0EYG to this finite etale cover of the complement of the regular effective Cartier divisor. It gives an affine etale neighborhood of y and finitely many standard punctured root covers with positive invertible exponents. Etale ascent preserves the regularity of the base; etale base change preserves divisor regularity; flatness preserves the nonzerodivisor equation.

Enumerate the finite factors by Fin m. Spec of a finite product is their disjoint union, and localization at the common equation identifies the union of punctured root covers with its basic open. Pullback pasting identifies the original cover base change along psi followed by phi with this open, over Spec S. This gives gamma and the displayed compatibility. Off the divisor, use etale local splitting, equation 1 and exponents 1; the zero quotient is regular. Empty covers use m=0.

theorem GaloisCover.regular_divisor_punctured_root_chart
    {L U : Scheme.{u}} (i : U ⟶ L)
    (G : Type (u + 1)) [Group G] [Finite G] (W : GaloisCover G U)
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (φ : Spec R ⟶ L) (f : R)
    (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : R))
    [IsRegularRing R] (hf : IsSMulRegular R f)
    [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})]
    (β : pullback i φ ≅ Scheme.Opens.toScheme (X := Spec R) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f))
    (hβ : β.hom ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (X := Spec R) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f) = pullback.snd i φ)
    (y : Spec R) :
    ∃ (S : CommRingCat.{u}) (ψ : Spec S ⟶ Spec R) (z : Spec S),
      Etale ψ ∧ ψ z = y ∧
      ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : S) (e : Fin m → ℕ),
        (∀ k, 0 < e k ∧ IsUnit (e k : S)) ∧
        IsRegularRing S ∧ IsSMulRegular S g ∧
        IsRegularRing (S ⧸ Ideal.span {g}) ∧
        let N := Spec (CommRingCat.of (∀ k : Fin m,
          AdjoinRoot ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial S) ^ e k - Polynomial.C g)))
        let q := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap S (∀ k : Fin m,
            AdjoinRoot ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial S) ^ e k - Polynomial.C g))))
        let V : N.Opens := PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen
          (algebraMap S (∀ k : Fin m,
            AdjoinRoot ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial S) ^ e k - Polynomial.C g)) g)
        ∃ γ : pullback (W.π ≫ i) (ψ ≫ φ) ≅ V.toScheme,
          γ.hom ≫ V.ι ≫ q = pullback.snd (W.π ≫ i) (ψ ≫ φ)
